findings.summary: An enabled but incomplete GOV-AR sidecar configuration failed open.
findings.evidence: The injector represented GOV-AR enablement only through optional annotations, but the header-proxy Config had no explicit enabled bit. With govar-enabled=true and all endpoint/principal/signer/policy fields absent, govarConfigured() was false, so HTTP LLM requests and HTTPS CONNECT were forwarded without admission.

findings.summary: No synchronous native Envoy-compatible TLS gateway path existed.
findings.evidence: Configured governed HTTPS CONNECT was denied rather than admitted, routed and settled. Repository search found no ext_authz, ext_proc or equivalent synchronous Envoy integration invoking /v1/admit and /v1/settle. The required real Azure HTTPS path therefore could not execute through the implementation.

findings.summary: Signer identity was not bound to authoritative workload and governance state.
findings.evidence: The per-principal signer derivation omitted namespace and there was no server-side workload registry. A valid signer could choose namespace, Team, Application, SensitiveData, AllowedZones, budget policy and routing policy in the signed request. The same signer authorized usage settlement and authoritative_unbilled cancellation. Derived signer provisioning for a newly assigned Pod UID also had no controller or exchange path.

findings.summary: Pod-controlled target filtering could bypass governed traffic.
findings.evidence: The provider target list came from a Pod annotation and both HTTP admission and governed CONNECT denial were conditioned on shouldInject(host). A workload could exclude its actual provider hostname and pass traffic through without GOV-AR.

findings.summary: The theorem-bearing fixed cohort was not preregistered or frozen.
findings.evidence: The database enforced only uniqueness of tenant/cohort_id/cohort_index. No registry fixed cohort membership, opportunity identities/features, size, weights or risk target before outcomes, so caller-selected cohort slots did not establish the Phase C common pre-outcome cohort assumption.

findings.summary: Approval was required but could not be consumed.
findings.evidence: Canary-enabled routing returned REQUIRE_APPROVAL, but no versioned approval reference or AIChangeRequest approval state could re-enter and pass admission. Approval-governed workloads dead-ended.

findings.summary: Budget-window renewal, rollover guards and carry allocation were absent.
findings.evidence: Budget identity changes failed closed whenever settled, reserved or carried exposure existed. This was safe locally but did not implement origin/current windows, provisional rollover guard, renewal, carried-debt payoff or historical correction attribution required by the state machine.

findings.summary: Strict-cap evidence and billable-category completeness were annotation assertions rather than verified provider controls.
findings.evidence: Output-cap verification, pricing version and freshness were mutable string annotations. The ledger represented only input/output token prices and did not introspect provider caps or cover cached input, reasoning, tools, media, retries and fallbacks. The conditional strict guarantee therefore lacked executable cap evidence.

findings.summary: Adaptive calibration and drift response had no online producer.
findings.evidence: Mean, margin, quantile, support, drift and cohort parameters were routing annotations. No calibration store, selected-feedback update, drift detector, revalidation workflow or immutable calibration artifact produced them. The real sidecar always marked rough input inexact, forcing non-strict methods to the strict context-window fallback.

findings.summary: Safety-critical configuration lacked typed validated API fields.
findings.evidence: Routability, pricing version/freshness, cap verification, latency, calibration, drift and risk allocation were unvalidated annotations rather than typed CRD fields with admission validation and status producers.

findings.summary: Durable lifecycle execution and reporting were incomplete.
findings.evidence: The transactional outbox table existed, but no durable outbox worker, expiry compare/cancel worker, unresolved resolver or rollover worker existed. Downward post-final corrections were made non-reusable by discarding their cost change rather than recording immutable audit credit and corrected origin-window reporting.

findings.summary: GOV-AR metrics, traces and structured transition audit remained absent.
findings.evidence: The service exposed the default Prometheus registry but no decision, hold, settlement, correction, unresolved, retry, fault or latency metrics and no trace propagation or immutable transition log suitable for E0-E7 evidence.

The proxy buffered the complete response and parsed one JSON object. Streaming/SSE behavior, usage extraction, cancellation and settlement semantics were not implemented and the response read was unbounded.

findings.summary: API and database compatibility remained fail-closed rather than migrated.
findings.evidence: The service correctly rejected nonempty legacy floating ledgers, but article3/infra/postgres/init.sql remained the old floating schema and /v1 cost fields were breaking. No reconciled conversion tool, versioned API compatibility path or tested upgrade/rollback procedure existed.
